object_description: long two-storey bar bordering the schoolyard, with a single-storey kindergarten set on an existing building
geometry_property: lowest floor sunk into the ground
single-storey volume on an existing roof
vertical facade structure with varying mesh
timber-concrete composite on a concrete base
design_condition: the bar borders the entire width of the schoolyard to the north, turned away from the historic wing and kept low by sinking its lowest gymnasium floor into the ground, with the kindergarten placed on the roof of an existing building

positive: The two-storey facade borders the entire width of the schoolyard and is cleverly turned away from the historic wing
The kindergarten on the roof of the existing building integrates the neighbouring apartment building
The kindergarten playground reaches the existing chestnut row and is shaded by it
A playground on all sides offers a village square-like atmosphere with a fountain
The entire lower level is reserved for games and sports with pitch, playing field and a grove-like play landscape
Extending the tree plantings strengthens the landscaped topographical edge and creates learning landscapes in partial shade
A new staircase and zig-zag footpath integrated into the embankment guarantee a threshold-free connection
Sinking the lowest gymnasium floor kept the new building low overall
The two learning clusters on the upper floor work
Access to the sports floors and their organisation is well placed
The vertical facade design with fine mesh on school floors and coarser mesh on the halls is interesting
The clusters implemented in the historic wing work well and interventions there are probably not particularly large
The depth of intervention in the second existing wing is rather low and its upper floor cluster is well implemented
The careful open space design ties the two levels together and responds harmoniously through tree planting
The placement creates a sheltered school square with a village square-like atmosphere
negative: Territorial problems are likely between the kindergarten playground and the nearby childcare rooms
The connecting stairs should be more generous given how many pupils will use the lower level
The length of the building hides the exits of stairs and ramp, not matching the importance of the connection
A more spacious entrance from the street was missed
Due to its length the large form appears imposing from north and west, reinforced by the vertical facade structure
The asphalt parking extending right up to the facades is not convincing as a prelude to the village
Repeating the same room structure on the ground floor for childcare and services is less convincing
Ground floor access is unfavourable, requiring a room-deep vestibule to be crossed
The facade design is not very site-specific
The auditorium is too small for the school and does not meet user requirements
Closing the half-storey vistas with checkrooms reduces transparency in the access area
The juxtaposition of teachers rooms, workrooms, workshops and storage seems random
The horizontal bracing is not shown
The settlement of the volume requires considerable excavation and pit stabilisation
The new building is out of scale with the street
The division of the spatial programme between new and existing buildings leaves something to be desired
The school square is somewhat secluded
